description: Newly woken and hard to rattle. She had most of it worked out by the second evening, and has not yet said how she feels about any of it.
lore: She woke and took it better than most, which she is aware is a strange thing to be good at. By her second evening she had worked the rest out unassisted: that the fire was kindness rather than answers, and that the people being kind were not going to explain the important part, because they do not know it either. She has asked good questions ever since, and has not once asked whether it is really true.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] came out from the stone house on her third morning, book open, the way she comes for everyone who will sit. The woman answered every question and then asked better ones back, which does not usually happen, and Bettany stayed past noon writing those down too. The last question, the gentle one — who she is waiting for — she was slowest to answer. What she said is not in the Chronicle; Bettany had already closed the book.

What she is, is hard to rattle. Not brave the way the tellers mean it when they are working a room — brave in the flat, unremarkable way of somebody who looks at a thing that should be frightening, decides how frightened to be, and is then that frightened and no more. Everybody in this country is waiting for something. She has not said what. She will get around to it.
gm_notes: Player-surrogate; her reason-for-staying stays deliberately blank, and Bettany closing the book keeps it off the record in-fiction as well, so quests can fill it later without contradiction.
